surprises.head: Los Angeles’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Los Angeles’s power play created 17.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.1 (about 6.6 against Ottawa) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: The Kings blow a four-goal lead, then win it in overtime
paras: Tyler Kleven opened the scoring for the Senators midway through the first. Erik Haula made it 1-1 for Los Angeles on the power play less than four minutes later. The second period belonged to the Kings. Trevor Moore, Mikey Anderson and Joel Armia scored three goals in just over four minutes early in the period to put the Kings up 4-1. Ottawa pulled Jonas Johansson after four goals and turned to Samuel Ersson for the rest of the second. The Kings’ Brandt Clarke left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Artemi Panarin made it 5-1 for the Kings on the power play late in the period. The third period belonged to the Senators. Dylan Cozens scored twice and Drake Batherson once in a little over five minutes early in the period to cut Los Angeles’ lead to 5-4. With the goalie pulled and less than two minutes left, Shane Pinto tied it up. Quinton Byfield won it in overtime. Four players had three-point nights: Drew Doughty with three assists, Batherson with a goal and two assists, the Sens’ Tim Stützle with three assists, and Cozens with two goals and an assist.

The Kings owned the chances, outshooting the Senators 38-22, and still had to sweat it out in overtime. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Kings win in regulation about seven in ten. Darcy Kuemper made 17 saves for the Kings.

Hayden Hodgson was thrown out with a game misconduct midway through the second. Nick Cousins and Samuel Helenius picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Kings moved to 4-6-2, seventh in the Pacific, while the Senators dropped to 8-5-1, slipping to fourth in the Atlantic.
